item.title: Bennett, Lee, Bettencourt earn key wins in court cases, allowing skilled veteran guards to lead Gonzaga basketball
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - MARCH 20: Ines Bettencourt #8 of the Gonzaga Bulldogs and Denim Deshields #22 of Ole Miss Rebels fight for possession of the ball in the second quarter during a first round game of the 2026 NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament held at Williams Arena on March 20, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Carlos Gonzalez/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Are you just done with all the court cases determining eligibility this year? So am I. As a result, I will translate this headline in a way that won’t give you a massive headache by just trying to understand what it all means. Here’s the headline: Thanks to a preliminary injunction granted by Santa Clara Superior Court Judge Beth McGowen, Gonzaga Bulldog point guards Xaivian Lee and Ines Bettencourt have been granted eligibility for a fifth year of eligibility, giving both Lee and Bettencourt another step closer to full eligibility for the 2026-27 year, as reported by CBS Sports’ Jon Rothstein and The Spokesman-Review’s Theo Lawson. However, the NCAA is going to appeal the decision, meaning the decision is not final in the case of Lee, Bettencourt, and more than 70 other players involved in the case who are seeking a fifth year through the NCAA’s new 5-in-5 rule. Translation into ten-year-old terms: Gonzaga wants really good and experienced point guards Xaivian Lee and Ines Bettencourt to play for them, and the big bad NCAA does not! However, a nice judge in California just stood up to the mighty evil NCAA and said no! This “no” is temporary, but until that’s resolved, Lee and Bettencourt can play! This whole circus is so exhausting. Alongside Lee and Bettencourt, Javon Bennett won a victory in his case to give him eligibility, while Chauncey Wiggins is still on his uphill battle (Izan Almansa is involved in a different case regarding professional players coming back for eligibility). Nonetheless, men’s coach Mark Few will have Xaivian Lee and Javon Bennett for the season, while women’s coach Lisa Fortier will have Ines Bettencourt. After all that mumbo-jumbo, both Few and Fortier will roster floor generals that bring the ability to swing a game on the court while providing veteran leadership that’s crucial to the success of both teams, who are expected to dominate the Pac-12 Conference in its first season of its second era. We will start on the men’s side with Lee and Bennett. I wrote about Lee’s impact on this Gonzaga squad alongside experienced French guard Nathan De Sousa last week, just because Lee and De Sousa were the only point guards on the team who were eligible. Bennett’s addition to the mix adds a lot of dimension to a very experienced trio of guards. Bennett committed to Gonzaga back on Aug. 5, around three weeks following the sudden departure of Mario Saint-Supery in July. It was clear that Bennett, who spent his last three years with Dayton and his freshman year at Merrimack, was on the radar of the Zags as one of the 5-in-5 transfers
item.content:encoded: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - MARCH 20: Ines Bettencourt #8 of the Gonzaga Bulldogs and Denim Deshields #22 of Ole Miss Rebels fight for possession of the ball in the second quarter during a first round game of the 2026 NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament held at Williams Arena on March 20, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Carlos Gonzalez/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Are you just done with all the court cases determining eligibility this year? So am I. As a result, I will translate this headline in a way that won’t give you a massive headache by just trying to understand what it all means. Here’s the headline: Thanks to a preliminary injunction granted by Santa Clara Superior Court Judge Beth McGowen, Gonzaga Bulldog point guards Xaivian Lee and Ines Bettencourt have been granted eligibility for a fifth year of eligibility, giving both Lee and Bettencourt another step closer to full eligibility for the 2026-27 year, as reported by CBS Sports’ Jon Rothstein and The Spokesman-Review’s Theo Lawson. However, the NCAA is going to appeal the decision, meaning the decision is not final in the case of Lee, Bettencourt, and more than 70 other players involved in the case who are seeking a fifth year through the NCAA’s new 5-in-5 rule. Translation into ten-year-old terms: Gonzaga wants really good and experienced point guards Xaivian Lee and Ines Bettencourt to play for them, and the big bad NCAA does not! However, a nice judge in California just stood up to the mighty evil NCAA and said no! This “no” is temporary, but until that’s resolved, Lee and Bettencourt can play! This whole circus is so exhausting. Alongside Lee and Bettencourt, Javon Bennett won a victory in his case to give him eligibility, while Chauncey Wiggins is still on his uphill battle (Izan Almansa is involved in a different case regarding professional players coming back for eligibility). Nonetheless, men’s coach Mark Few will have Xaivian Lee and Javon Bennett for the season, while women’s coach Lisa Fortier will have Ines Bettencourt. After all that mumbo-jumbo, both Few and Fortier will roster floor generals that bring the ability to swing a game on the court while providing veteran leadership that’s crucial to the success of both teams, who are expected to dominate the Pac-12 Conference in its first season of its second era. We will start on the men’s side with Lee and Bennett. I wrote about Lee’s impact on this Gonzaga squad alongside experienced French guard Nathan De Sousa last week, just because Lee and De Sousa were the only point guards on the team who were eligible. Bennett’s addition to the mix adds a lot of dimension to a very experienced trio of guards. Bennett committed to Gonzaga back on Aug. 5, around three weeks following the sudden departure of Mario Saint-Supery in July. It was clear that Bennett, who spent his last three years with Dayton and his freshman year at Merrimack, was on the radar of the Zags as one of the 5-in-5 transfers that Few wanted. When I dove into the film, I could see why. Bennett averaged nearly 16 points, 3 assists, and 1.5 steals per game last year, leading the Flyers in scoring and assists. Listed at 5-10, 165, Bennett is undersized, but like all good undersized guards, he uses this to his advantage. He’s lightning quick and a tough finisher around the rim, which he will need against Pac-12 frontcourts. He’s also a stalwart defender at his position; in his freshman year, he averaged 2.9 steals per game at Merrimack, which ranked second in the nation. What stood out to me most, however, was Bennett’s late-game availability. He hit multiple clutch shots down the stretch of games last year for Dayton (many of which are highlighted in the video above), showcasing an uncanny ability to size up defenders and take them one-on-one. Also, Bennett shot 89.8% from the free-throw line last year, which will earn him a spot on the court in every late-game situation. This will be a massive addition to this offense, especially if Bennett comes off the bench (which he likely will), and can become an offensive engine in the second unit for Few. What stood out to me most, however, was Bennett’s late-game availability. He hit multiple clutch shots down the stretch of games last year for Dayton (many of which are highlighted in the video above), showcasing an uncanny ability to size up defenders and take them one-on-one. Also, Bennett shot 89.8% from the free-throw line last year, which will earn him a spot on the court in every late-game situation. This will be a massive addition to this offense, especially if Bennett comes off the bench (which he likely will), and can become an offensive engine in the second unit for Few. Yet, Bennett’s efficiency numbers do stick out. He shot 39% from the field and 34% from three last season, a result of him being the No. 1 scoring option on the team as a 5-10 guard. In our latest episode of Bulldog Business with Josh Gilchrist , I compared Bennett to Fred VanVleet, who consistently shoots at or under 40% from the field during the season. Both are undersized guards who are tenacious defenders, skilled at taking defenders one-on-one, and are reliable guards in late-game scenarios. While the size and the comfortability of being moved from the No. 1 option to a sixth man role (RE: Braeden Smith last year, now with Notre Dame) can be a concern, Bennett will prove to be vital to this team’s success, especially down the stretch of games. Watch out for Bennett in the Sixth Man of the Year conversations this year in the Pac-12. Now Few has Lee and Bennett, two guards who have played four years of college basketball and been their team’s No. 1 scoring option before. It will be interesting to see how the Hall of Fame coach tinkers with lineups, but the experience in the backcourt with those two and De Sousa is extremely exciting. On to the women’s side, where Ines Bettencourt secured a victory in her 5-in-5 case, which also applied to Lee. With Bettencourt’s eligibility settled, seven-time WCC Coach of the Year winner Fortier now returns all five starters from last year’s WCC Tournament title squad, a tremendous feat in today’s college basketball landscape. Bettencourt, a 5-9 point guard from Sao Miguel, Portugal, spent her first two years with UConn, playing less than 10 minutes per game each year before transferring to Gonzaga. Last year, Bettencourt started all 33 games, averaging 6.3 points, 3.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.5 steals per contest. The veteran guard is also the vocal leader of this group and will be the most experienced Zag on the roster this season. On the court, similarly to Bennett, Bettencourt is a tenacious defender and loves pushing the pace on the offensive end off of steals and tip-outs in the halfcourt. This creates a multi-dimensional system for an offense that led the nation in 3-point shooting last year at 39.6%. While Bettencourt’s 3-point shooting numbers were down last year compared to her first year in a Zag uniform, her presence as the lead guard with reigning WCC Player of the Year Lauren Whittaker and two-time First-Team all-WCC guard Allie Turner will likely anchor a dominant force in the Pac-12 this season. The women’s team is returning 10 (!!!) total players from last season’s roster that finished 24-10 and 14-4 in conference play. Going into last season, the story was about how Fortier was going to handle eight total newcomers going into the year. Now that script has flipped, and it’s going to be entertainment night in and night out from this squad. Because of these court case wins that granted Lee, Bennett, and Bettencourt their long-awaited eligibility, Zag basketball fans will be delighted to see an array of experience and talent anchor their teams this season as the Pac-12’s new horizon is inching ever closer.

item.title: Fennville earns historic win with sensational touchdown pass from nose tackle
item.description: FENNVILLE - Senior night is a little extra special for the Fennville football team. Being ineligible or the playoffs, the seniors season ended Friday night. But was it ever memorable. Fennville coach Wendell Hughes put in an all-senior lineup to start the game, which included 275-pound nose tackle Omar Martinez lined up at quarterback. He took the snap and ran up the left side - the old "student-body left" - and rumbled 30 yards for a first down as the crowd went wild. Turns out, that was just the appetizer. A couple plays later, Martinez was back in at quarterback and launched the ball 47 yards into the hands of senior receiver Jesse Bernard for a touchdown. It is a memory Martinez, Bernard and the entire senior class will never forget made even better by the 42-22 win over Marcellus on Friday , Oct. 23. More: Week 9 high school football live scoreboard and roundup for Holland area "It means a lot to us to finish with a win on senior night," Martinez said. "I am so surprised it worked that well. The guys blocked really well (to make it happen). I'll never forget this." Neither will his teammates, especially knowing it was the last game for the seniors. "It makes this game everything. This is my last time playing with my friends from kindergarten. It is unexplainable how much this means. We couldn't end on a better note," senior Ashton "Happy" Senters said. "I don't think words can explain the memory of Omar throwing that touchdown made me so much happier than I have ever been. I will probably be telling this story to my kids." The fun formation came from something Hughes saw in practice. "I told them I would start all seniors. We were messing around before practice and he threw one a country mile. I asked him to do that again and he was throwing dimes. My wheels started spinning," Hughes said. "We were going to run the ball first, then throw, but we had a penalty on the second play. Then I went back to the regular offense, and it was really itching at me. So we tried it and I was tickled for the seniors. I was so happy it worked like it did. Fennville finished the season 6-3, defeating a ranked team in the finale. The Blackhawks put together back-to-back winning seasons for the first time since 2017-18 and ninth time in the past 47 seasons. It is Fennville's 17th six-win season. It was the sixth time the Blackhawks scored more than 300 points and eighth time they scored 100 or more points more than their opponents. Seamus Lynch scored on a direct snap and Mason Sabala hit Bernard for the conversion with 6:55 to go in the half, pulling the Blackhawks within 16-14. Sabala marched the Blackhawks the length of the field and ran in a 2-yard keeper with 1:11 to go in the half. The conversion missed but Fennville led 20-16. On the first drive of the second half, Sabala threw a 34-yard touchdown to Lynch on fourth-and-11. Bernard's conversion pushed the Blackhawks lead to 28-16. After a Marcellus score, Fennville scored on a pitch from Sabala to Bernard
item.content:encoded: FENNVILLE - Senior night is a little extra special for the Fennville football team. Being ineligible or the playoffs, the seniors season ended Friday night. But was it ever memorable. Fennville coach Wendell Hughes put in an all-senior lineup to start the game, which included 275-pound nose tackle Omar Martinez lined up at quarterback. He took the snap and ran up the left side - the old "student-body left" - and rumbled 30 yards for a first down as the crowd went wild. Turns out, that was just the appetizer. A couple plays later, Martinez was back in at quarterback and launched the ball 47 yards into the hands of senior receiver Jesse Bernard for a touchdown. It is a memory Martinez, Bernard and the entire senior class will never forget made even better by the 42-22 win over Marcellus on Friday , Oct. 23. More: Week 9 high school football live scoreboard and roundup for Holland area "It means a lot to us to finish with a win on senior night," Martinez said. "I am so surprised it worked that well. The guys blocked really well (to make it happen). I'll never forget this." Neither will his teammates, especially knowing it was the last game for the seniors. "It makes this game everything. This is my last time playing with my friends from kindergarten. It is unexplainable how much this means. We couldn't end on a better note," senior Ashton "Happy" Senters said. "I don't think words can explain the memory of Omar throwing that touchdown made me so much happier than I have ever been. I will probably be telling this story to my kids." The fun formation came from something Hughes saw in practice. "I told them I would start all seniors. We were messing around before practice and he threw one a country mile. I asked him to do that again and he was throwing dimes. My wheels started spinning," Hughes said. "We were going to run the ball first, then throw, but we had a penalty on the second play. Then I went back to the regular offense, and it was really itching at me. So we tried it and I was tickled for the seniors. I was so happy it worked like it did. Fennville finished the season 6-3, defeating a ranked team in the finale. The Blackhawks put together back-to-back winning seasons for the first time since 2017-18 and ninth time in the past 47 seasons. It is Fennville's 17th six-win season. It was the sixth time the Blackhawks scored more than 300 points and eighth time they scored 100 or more points more than their opponents. Seamus Lynch scored on a direct snap and Mason Sabala hit Bernard for the conversion with 6:55 to go in the half, pulling the Blackhawks within 16-14. Sabala marched the Blackhawks the length of the field and ran in a 2-yard keeper with 1:11 to go in the half. The conversion missed but Fennville led 20-16. On the first drive of the second half, Sabala threw a 34-yard touchdown to Lynch on fourth-and-11. Bernard's conversion pushed the Blackhawks lead to 28-16. After a Marcellus score, Fennville scored on a pitch from Sabala to Bernard early in the fourth quarter. The conversion pass to Bernard was good and the lead was 36-22 with 11:08 to go. Senior Ashton Senters came up with a huge tackle for a 9-yard loss then fellow senior Israel Arredondo added another on fourth down to give the Blackhawks the ball. Senters then recovered a fumble to seal it then scored on an 11-yard run with 2:11 to go and a 42-22 lead. Brandon Lavery added a late interception. Fennville's seniors are Martinez, Bernard, Kaiden Atteberry, Gavin Beltran, Riley Campbell, Khordell Bernard, Senters, Nolan Menear, Lavery, Arredondo and Calvin Giles, who also had his senior night for marching band. "This was their playoff game. We have been saying that all week," Hughes said. Why Fennville can't make the playoffs While many teams with winning records have the excitement in anticipation of making the playoffs, and who they will face. For two years in a row, that hasn't been the Fennville football team, despite a winning record. That is because the Blackhawks dropped down to 8-person football a few years ago. Since Fennville High School is technically too big for 8-player, the team cannot make the playoffs. Even if they were eligible, 8-person football usually requires a 7-2 record to make the playoffs since it has fewer rounds. It is a tough deal, but one the school administration made to make sure football didn't evaporate in Fennville with numbers in the program dropping to an all-time low. That means every Week 9, the Blackhawks are playing their final game of the season, whether they are 9-0 or 0-9. The first few years, it wasn't a disappointment because the Blackhawks weren't going to make the playoffs anyway. "It is disappointing we don't get that opportunity. We are trying to get back to 11-man, but to have a program garner some success, we have to stay in 8-man right now," Hughes said. But the Blackhawks have had back-to-back winning seasons for the first time in a decade. The recent success of the program could lead to more numbers in the youth football programs in the area and could eventually lead Fennville back to 11-person football - and eventually the playoffs. But there is a certain specialness to the finality of each Fennville season - especially this one. "It is a rallying cry for our seniors. Last year, we made the trip all the way up to Onaway on Week 9. We stayed overnight and the boys will have great memories from that for the rest of their lives," Hughes said. "We were at home this year." Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter @DanDAddona or Facebook @HollandSentinelSport s. item.title: Five takeaways from UVA football’s last-minute 19-16 loss to Duke
item.description: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 23: Jekail Middlebrook #21 of the Virginia Cavaliers carries the ball during a game between the Virginia Cavaliers and the Duke Blue Devils at Scott Stadium on October 23, 2026 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images After having its College Football Playoff dreams crushed last year, Virginia got its chance at redemption Friday night in the long-anticipated rematch of the ACC Championship Game. The last time these teams met, in Charlotte in December, Duke won 27-20 in overtime after a Virginia trick play was intercepted, giving the Blue Devils their first league title since 1962. This time the ‘Hoos were at home, where they had won five straight and looked like a different team. They opened and closed as 2.5-point favorites. This was in spite of the fact that they were still shorthanded, without receivers Kameron Courtney and Rico Flores Jr. and safeties Brandyn Hillman, Ethan Minter and Corey Costner. For a half, it looked like the crowd would get its revenge. Duke went 78 yards in four plays for a touchdown on its opening drive, but quarterback Walker Eget hurt his hand on the first big throw of that drive and did not return until halftime. Virginia answered with a Jekail Middlebrook direct-snap touchdown, added two Will Bettridge field goals and took a 13-7 lead into the locker room after holding the ball for more than 20 minutes of the first half. Eget came back for the second half, and Duke methodically chipped away with two Gavin Strange field goals. Bettridge’s 30-yarder put Virginia back in front 16-13 with three minutes left, but Duke went 75 yards in seven plays and won it on a double pass, with running back Nate Sheppard throwing 28 yards to a wide-open Brody Keefe with 1:14 to play. Strange missed the extra point, and it didn’t matter. Beau Pribula’s last desperation heave was intercepted, dropping Virginia to 4-4 (2-3 ACC), with its first home loss of the season and its first back-to-back losses since the end of 2024. Here are my five takeaways from the loss. Virginia’s conservative coaching decisions came back to bite it Virginia outgained Duke 353-327, won the first-down battle 22-16 and held the ball for 38:47 to Duke’s 21:13. item.content:encoded: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 23: Jekail Middlebrook #21 of the Virginia Cavaliers carries the ball during a game between the Virginia Cavaliers and the Duke Blue Devils at Scott Stadium on October 23, 2026 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images After having its College Football Playoff dreams crushed last year, Virginia got its chance at redemption Friday night in the long-anticipated rematch of the ACC Championship Game. The last time these teams met, in Charlotte in December, Duke won 27-20 in overtime after a Virginia trick play was intercepted, giving the Blue Devils their first league title since 1962. This time the ‘Hoos were at home, where they had won five straight and looked like a different team. They opened and closed as 2.5-point favorites. This was in spite of the fact that they were still shorthanded, without receivers Kameron Courtney and Rico Flores Jr. and safeties Brandyn Hillman, Ethan Minter and Corey Costner. For a half, it looked like the crowd would get its revenge. Duke went 78 yards in four plays for a touchdown on its opening drive, but quarterback Walker Eget hurt his hand on the first big throw of that drive and did not return until halftime. Virginia answered with a Jekail Middlebrook direct-snap touchdown, added two Will Bettridge field goals and took a 13-7 lead into the locker room after holding the ball for more than 20 minutes of the first half. Eget came back for the second half, and Duke methodically chipped away with two Gavin Strange field goals. Bettridge’s 30-yarder put Virginia back in front 16-13 with three minutes left, but Duke went 75 yards in seven plays and won it on a double pass, with running back Nate Sheppard throwing 28 yards to a wide-open Brody Keefe with 1:14 to play. Strange missed the extra point, and it didn’t matter. Beau Pribula’s last desperation heave was intercepted, dropping Virginia to 4-4 (2-3 ACC), with its first home loss of the season and its first back-to-back losses since the end of 2024. Here are my five takeaways from the loss. Virginia’s conservative coaching decisions came back to bite it Virginia outgained Duke 353-327, won the first-down battle 22-16 and held the ball for 38:47 to Duke’s 21:13. However, Virginia simply refused to deliver the finishing blow. The first chance to bury Duke came while Eget was sidelined. Redshirt freshman Dan Mahan played the rest of the first half, and Duke’s four drives with him at quarterback went 15 plays for 36 yards and four punts. Virginia scored 13 points over that stretch, but only seven of them came in the end zone. On its second scoring drive, the ‘Hoos got inside the Duke 10, then had to burn a timeout to avoid a delay-of-game penalty on third-and-goal from about the 6, a timeout that would have come in handy at the end of the half. What came out of the timeout was a run up the middle for two yards and a 21-yard field goal, a call that even left the announcers confused. It was the first of several conservative calls that drew questions from the broadcast. The end of the half was worse. With 37 seconds left, a timeout in hand and third-and-3 in field-goal range, Tony Elliott played for the kick. The crowd booed, and it had reason to. Duke had a backup quarterback, a banged-up secondary and no momentum, and Virginia let it go into the locker room down only six. It was as if Elliott hadn’t even considered the possibility that Eget might not be done for the game and that this game could be won by simply not turning the ball over. The same caution showed up once again in the fourth quarter. Leading 13-10 and pinned at its own 5, Virginia ran on first down, rolled Pribula out with about two receivers in the pattern for a throwaway, and handed the ball to Xay Davis for a loss on third down. The boos came again. The predictability of the Virginia offense has almost become its calling card. To play devil’s advocate, in a rare moment of creativity from the offense in the third quarter, Virginia called a double pass that got Middlebrook wide open, but the ball never came out, which is all the more ironic knowing how the game was eventually won. A few plays later, Pribula was sacked and Bettridge’s 47-yard try sailed wide right. Duke ran its own double pass on the final drive, but this time Sheppard connected with a wide-open receiver for the game-winning score. For the second straight meeting, the difference was a trick play, and for the second straight meeting it went Duke’s way. The defense did all it could, led by Maddox Marcellus and a familiar Kam Robinson Sheppard came in leading the ACC and ranking third nationally at 136.7 rushing yards per game. He finished with 55 on 15 carries, and 32 of those came on one run on the opening drive. His other 14 carries went for 23 yards. Duke ran for 71 yards as a team, went 2-for-10 on third down and punted six times. Marcellus was Virginia’s best player. He had four tackles, all solo, two of them for loss, and a pass breakup. He dropped Sheppard behind the line on the first play of Duke’s second drive, and on Duke’s opening drive of the second half, after a 31-yard one-handed catch by Jared Richardson that survived a review, Marcellus broke up a throw into the end zone and then swallowed a Sheppard screen. Duke settled for a field goal. Montino Williams had a strong night too, with five tackles, a pass breakup, a perfectly timed delayed blitz on that same drive and a stop on a third-down draw two yards short of the sticks in the first quarter. Then there’s Kam Robinson, who finally looked like the old Kam Robinson. Spying Mahan on third-and-6 in the second quarter, he ran him down for his first sack of the season. In the third quarter, he got his hands on a ball that looked like it was going to be caught, batted it into the air and caught it himself for his first interception of the season. Both plays ended Duke drives. It was his first interception since his pick-six at California on Nov. 1, 2025, two weeks before he tore his ACL at Duke. It wasn’t perfect. Eget threw for 211 yards in barely more than a half of football, and four completions of 28 yards or more (35 to Jonah Burton, 31 to Richardson, 43 to Jake Taylor and the 28-yard touchdown to Keefe) accounted for 137 of Duke’s 256 passing yards. With the game on the line, Duke went 75 yards in 1:46. But a defense missing three safeties held a team averaging 31.7 points per game to 19. Jekail Middlebrook set a career high, and the direct snap keeps working I have called UVA out in the past for going away from Middlebrook seemingly for no reason when things were working. On Friday, Middlebrook ran 24 times for 117 yards and a touchdown. Both numbers were season highs by a wide margin (his previous bests were 17 carries and 95 yards against Syracuse), and the 117 yards topped his previous career high of 109, set at Middle Tennessee against Kennesaw State last season. It was his first 100-yard game in a Virginia uniform. It came against a Duke run defense that entered 18th nationally, allowing 92.5 yards per game and 3.2 yards per carry, and had given up only 11 runs of 10 yards or more all season. Middlebrook had a 20-yard toss that opened Virginia’s touchdown drive and a 21-yard run up the middle late in the second quarter. With Duke playing a lot of man coverage, there was room to run. After abandoning the run in the second half at SMU, offensive coordinator Des Kitchings stuck with it for 60 minutes this time. The direct snap remains Virginia’s most reliable short-yardage play for the second straight year. After a second-down direct snap left Middlebrook just short of the goal line and a quarterback sneak was stuffed, Virginia brought in heavy personnel and snapped it to him again on fourth-and-goal for the touchdown, Virginia’s only one of the game. item.title: Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet out for season after knee injury; fans react to loss
item.description: The Chicago Bears will be without tight end Cole Kmet for the rest of the season after he suffered a right knee injury during the fourth quarter of Thursday night's game against the New England Patriots . The Bears have not provided details about the nature of the injury. ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch Kmet, 27, was injured late in the game and was later carted off the field. His absence comes as the Bears offense has been gaining momentum following the return of quarterback Caleb Williams from a hamstring injury. "It's a tough loss, definitely. Bears fans are going to be really thinking about that. You know, he stepped up big last year, too, with some major catches for us," Bears fan Gustavo Baptista Defaria said at Weather Mark Tavern in the South Loop. Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet grabs his knee after getting tackled by the New England Patriots. AP Photo/Jeffrey Phelps Bears coach Ben Johnson expressed disappointment over the injury. "It stinks. It does. I hate it for him. I hate it for his teammates as well," Johnson said. Now in his seventh season with the Bears, Kmet is the longest-tenured player on the roster. Among Bears tight ends, he ranks second only to Mike Ditka in receptions and receiving yards. SEE ALSO | ABC7 Sports Overtime with Dionne Miller: Oct. 23, 2026 A native of Chicago's northwest suburbs, Kmet attended St. Viator High School and has become one of the team's most visible players in the community, making him a fan favorite. Dave Archibald, Kmet's high school football coach at St. Viator, said he expects the tight end to remain a strong presence for his teammates during his recovery. "He'll be the best teammate that he can be and continue to be a great teammate to every in his position group and love the city that loves him and go into the rehab full go. I have no doubt," Archibald said. Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet gives a thumbs up after getting tackled by the New England Patriots in Chicago, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. Kmet was hurt on the play. AP Photo/Jeffrey Phelps With Kmet sidelined, other players at the position are expected to take on larger roles, including second-year tight end Colston Loveland and rookie tight end Sam Roush. Despite the setback, some fans expressed confidence in the team's ability to adjust. "I have a lot of faith in Ben Johnson. I mean, you know, I'm sure he's going to spin up someone. I'm sure we have the right backup," Bears fan Vishal Shah said. "It's a team sport, so hopefully everybody comes back, and as a team gets together, and we'll get there," Bears fan Mendkhuu Enkhbayar said. Kmet's injury comes at a pivotal point in the season. The Bears are 5-2 and continue to chase the Minnesota Vikings, who sit atop the NFC North at 5-0.

item.description: Game 1 of the 2026 World Series is officially in the books, with the Milwaukee Brewers taking down the Tampa Bay Rays in a nail-biter. Things won't slow down between the Rays and Brewers, who will meet again on Saturday at 8 p.m. ET for Game 2. Ahead of Saturday's action, get everything you need to know below, including TV/streaming information, the full World Series schedule and more. 2026 World Series Predictions: Rays vs. Brewers picks, MVP favorites and biggest X-factors The Rays and Brewers are both chasing their first World Series championship. Our Rotoworld experts break down the matchup, identify potential difference-makers and make their picks. D.J. Short , Matthew Pouliot , +1 More How to watch Rays vs. Brewers 2026 World Series Game 2 When: Saturday, Oct. 24 Where: American Family Field - Milwaukee, Wisconsin Time: 8:00 p.m. ET TV: FOX, FOX Deportes Streaming: FOX One Rays vs. Brewers 2026 World Series schedule and results Game 1 : Brewers 3 , Rays 2 Game 2 : Saturday, Oct. 24 - 8:00 p.m. ET - at Brewers Game 3 : Monday, Oct. 26 - 8:00 p.m. ET - at Rays Game 4 : Tuesday, Oct. 27 - 8:00 p.m. ET - at Rays *Game 5 : Wednesday, Oct. 28 - 8:00 p.m. ET - at Rays *Game 6 : Friday, Oct. 30 - 8:00 p.m. ET - at Brewers *Game 7 : Saturday, Oct. 31 - 8:00 p.m. ET - at Brewers * = if necessary Rays vs. Brewers Game 2 2026 World Series projected lineups The starting lineups for Game 2 of the 2026 World Series are TBD. Rays vs. Brewers Game 2 2026 MLB World Series probable pitchers Brewers : Logan Henderson Rays : Drew Rasmussen Rays vs. Brewers Game 2 2026 World Series betting odds Milwaukee Brewers: -122 Tampa Bay Rays: +102 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Have the Milwaukee Brewers ever won a World Series? The Brewers have never won a World Series, having lost their only prior appearance in 1982 (defeated by the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games). Have the Tampa Bay Rays ever won a World Series? The Rays are 0-2 across their two World Series appearances, with losses to the Dodgers in 2020 (4-2) and Phillies in 2008 (4-1). How many games are in the World Series? The World Series is a best-of-seven series. The first team to win four games wins the series.

item.title: Five Takeaways from Mizzou’s 71-67 exhibition win at Kansas State
item.description: MANHATTAN, KS - OCTOBER 23: Forward Toni Bryant #14 of the Missouri Tigers scores with a dun in the first half against the Kansas State Wildcats at Bramlage Coliseum on October 23, 2026 in Manhattan, Kansas. (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mizzou Basketball won an exhibition game in Manhattan, Kansas tonight. Even though the game didn’t count, the last time a win in Bramlage happened for the Tigers was in February of 2004. So 22 years is a minute. I don’t mean to bring that up to make it a bigger deal than it is. Bramlage wasn’t full, Kansas State is expected to be amongst the worst teams in the Big 12 this year, but it’s also been a place where we’ve watched the Tigers march into only to be slaughtered. So winning there, in any manner, feels nice. Even if it doesn’t count. Here’s the screen cap of the Statbroadcast box: Everyone played some kind of minutes except Jaylen Carey, Nicholas Randall, and CJ Gunn. Trent Burns played 3 minutes, Luke Northweather played 4, Aaron Rowe played 5, and Jamier Jones played 8. Mark Mitchell played 16 minutes and didn’t make a shot, and Trent Pierce only played 15 minutes but scored 10 points. It was clear Dennis Gates was in the crash lab late. Mitchell was off the floor the final 10 minutes, Pierce was off the floor for the final 12 minutes. When Mark left the floor for the last time Missouri had a 9 point lead. Down the stretch it was a combination of Jason Crowe, Jr., Kennard Davis, Jr., Aidan Chronister, Cord Stansberry, Toni Bryant, and Bryson Tiller. And after Mitchell came out, there were 5 substitutions. So it was clear what the goal was. Get these young guys the experience of closing out a game on the road. So with that said, here are some quick takeaways: Jason Crowe, Jr. looks the part The 5-star McDonald’s All American had some rocky moments, but with 21 points on 18 shots, 5 assists, 3 steals and just a couple turnovers, he looked about what you had hoped. Crowe was off from distance, connecting on just one of his six three point attempts. But the rest of his game was in full effect. There were a few times when Crowe was given the ball during, what can only be described with the Benny Hill theme song, and he made the bad call to forge ahead into traffic and only made things worse. That’s part of the growth with a freshman point guard who is not really a point guard. There are going to be moments where you aren’t sure what he’s doing. But otherwise, Crowe was terrific. Mark Mitchell looks a bit rusty It’s not surprising, but we didn’t see the best version of Mark Mitchell. He’s still got a ways to go to be fully acclimated, plus with the jostling between campus and court, it might take him some time to get back to the Mark Mitchell we’ve been accustomed to. Of all the guys on the roster, he’s the one I’m least worried about. It might take time for him to find his exact role, but I doubt there are going to be a lot of nights like this one for the 5th year senior. Defense? At Missou
item.content:encoded: MANHATTAN, KS - OCTOBER 23: Forward Toni Bryant #14 of the Missouri Tigers scores with a dun in the first half against the Kansas State Wildcats at Bramlage Coliseum on October 23, 2026 in Manhattan, Kansas. (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mizzou Basketball won an exhibition game in Manhattan, Kansas tonight. Even though the game didn’t count, the last time a win in Bramlage happened for the Tigers was in February of 2004. So 22 years is a minute. I don’t mean to bring that up to make it a bigger deal than it is. Bramlage wasn’t full, Kansas State is expected to be amongst the worst teams in the Big 12 this year, but it’s also been a place where we’ve watched the Tigers march into only to be slaughtered. So winning there, in any manner, feels nice. Even if it doesn’t count. Here’s the screen cap of the Statbroadcast box: Everyone played some kind of minutes except Jaylen Carey, Nicholas Randall, and CJ Gunn. Trent Burns played 3 minutes, Luke Northweather played 4, Aaron Rowe played 5, and Jamier Jones played 8. Mark Mitchell played 16 minutes and didn’t make a shot, and Trent Pierce only played 15 minutes but scored 10 points. It was clear Dennis Gates was in the crash lab late. Mitchell was off the floor the final 10 minutes, Pierce was off the floor for the final 12 minutes. When Mark left the floor for the last time Missouri had a 9 point lead. Down the stretch it was a combination of Jason Crowe, Jr., Kennard Davis, Jr., Aidan Chronister, Cord Stansberry, Toni Bryant, and Bryson Tiller. And after Mitchell came out, there were 5 substitutions. So it was clear what the goal was. Get these young guys the experience of closing out a game on the road. So with that said, here are some quick takeaways: Jason Crowe, Jr. looks the part The 5-star McDonald’s All American had some rocky moments, but with 21 points on 18 shots, 5 assists, 3 steals and just a couple turnovers, he looked about what you had hoped. Crowe was off from distance, connecting on just one of his six three point attempts. But the rest of his game was in full effect. There were a few times when Crowe was given the ball during, what can only be described with the Benny Hill theme song, and he made the bad call to forge ahead into traffic and only made things worse. That’s part of the growth with a freshman point guard who is not really a point guard. There are going to be moments where you aren’t sure what he’s doing. But otherwise, Crowe was terrific. Mark Mitchell looks a bit rusty It’s not surprising, but we didn’t see the best version of Mark Mitchell. He’s still got a ways to go to be fully acclimated, plus with the jostling between campus and court, it might take him some time to get back to the Mark Mitchell we’ve been accustomed to. Of all the guys on the roster, he’s the one I’m least worried about. It might take time for him to find his exact role, but I doubt there are going to be a lot of nights like this one for the 5th year senior. Defense? At Missouri, Dennis Gates has yet to field a top 50 defense. In fact his best defense was 68th. This unit looks like it could be different. For all the bumps they had offensively, the defense was excellent for most of the night. They came out of the gates a little iffy, but they locked down for the rest of the half, and opened the game up with their D to start the second half. I’ll update this post with the official study hall graphics later, but if you’re looking at intensity, blocks, steals, deflections, they did it all. Toni Bryant played like a freshman Bryant played 24 minutes, and had 6 points on 2-6 shooting. But just 1 of 4 from behind the arc. And two of those shots I didn’t care for. He’s a good shooter when it’s a catch and shoot, but he’s got to learn that it’s ok to pass up a shot if there’s a hesitation or a fumbled catch. Still you have to like his energy on defense, and he had 2 blocked shots. But needs to get more rebounds. Relax on Bryson Tiller Tiller was pretty bad offensively. He was pretty good offensively at the Mizzou Pro Day. He’s figuring that part of his game out in a lot of ways. But what he is already is a pretty good defender, and a tough physical presence inside. He had 9 rebounds and 5 blocks! That’s tough. He had 5 turnovers too! That’s not good. If there’s one thing about Gates, is he’s been really good about figuring out how best to deploy his players to generate offense. That part with Tiller is still a work in progress. But the defensive side of certainly something to be hopfeul about. I’ll post Study Hall here when I have it. But that’s about as much as you can take away from this game. It was weird, Dennis Gates used a ton of lineups, he didn’t run his big dogs out there much, and massaged a win with three freshmen on the floor for most of the closing minutes. You take it. I’m looking forward to the games that count.

item.title: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum quiets the external noise with clutch performance vs. Knicks
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Celtics’ Jayson Tatum quiets the external noise with clutch performance vs. Knicks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum delivered the perfect response to questions about his post-injury explosiveness. Je scored 36 points to lead the Boston Celtics past the defending champion New York Knicks, 107-103, on Friday night at TD Garden. After an uneven season opener against Detroit fueled doubts about his conditioning following a prolonged Achilles rehabilitation, Tatum looked every bit like Boston’s franchise cornerstone . JAYSON TATUM WITH BACK-TO-BACK CLUTCH BUCKETS TO SECURE THE WIN FOR THE CELTICS 😤 pic.twitter.com/hexgwSPogm — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 24, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He shot an outstanding 14-of-20 from the field, including 25 points in the second half. That was before taking over during a tense fourth-quarter finish. New York erased most of Boston’s 12-point advantage, cutting the deficit to 99-98. Tatum then answered with a clutch 19-foot jumper with 1:11 remaining, then delivered the decisive blow with a step-back three-pointer. Tatum accounted for seven of Boston’s final eight points. He shut down the Knicks’ comeback bid and gave the Celtics a statement victory early in the 2026-27 season. With Jaylen Brown now in Philadelphia , Boston needs Tatum to shoulder an even greater offensive burden. His performance against New York offered an emphatic reminder that he remains capable of delivering when the pressure peaks. Tatum’s season began with questions after his inconsistent showing in Detroit. Friday’s explosion, though, provided a timely answer. His efficient shooting, aggressive scoring, and composure in crunch time suggested that his lengthy recovery has not erased the qualities that make him Boston’s centerpiece. As the Celtics adjust to a reconfigured roster, Tatum’s ability to control late-game possessions will be crucial. One win cannot settle every concern, but his performance against the reigning champions offered Boston a promising foundation for its new era. Related: Celtics HC Joe Mazzulla gives defensive props to Jayson Tatum, Jordan Walsh after win over Knicks Related: Watch Celtics’ Jayson Tatum reveal his stunned reaction to the Jaylen Brown trade

item.title: Brewers win first World Series game in 44 years, Game 2 ticket prices are soaring
item.description: Milwaukee has won its first World Series game in 44 years. The Brewers held on for a thrilling 3-2 win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1, grabbing a 1-0 lead in the 2026 World Series . It's a quick turnaround for Game 2, scheduled for Saturday night in Milwaukee and ticket prices are not getting any cheaper. SHOP : World Series Game 2 tickets The Brewers jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the first inning and thanks to a stellar team pitching performance never relinquished the lead, despite the Rays mounting a 9th inning comeback. Limited tickets for Game 2 are still available, but time is running out. Here's everything you need to know in order to join the loudest crowd Milwaukee has ever seen and buy last-minute tickets to Game 2 of the World Series . Shop World Series Game 2 tickets Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays World Series Game 2 tickets While ticket prices for Game 1 fell in the days leading up to the start of the World Series, Game 2 ticket prices have actually increased on Friday, up almost $500 from their morning price. item.title: Bowman makes Ohio history as Shelby cruises to third straight 10-0 season
item.description: SHELBY — It was a history-making kind of night at the Whippet Athletic Complex. Shelby senior wideout Brady Bowman caught seven passes for 151 yards and one touchdown to move from 10the to eighth place on the Ohio High School Athletic Association's all-time career receiving yards list. With these numbers, he surpassed the 4,000 career yards mark and now sits at 4,114 and counting. Shelby’s team dominance helped lead it to a 42-7 victory over Marion Harding. HOW'D WE DO? WEEK 10 PICKS All tied up with one week of high school football left “It is an unreal feeling to be on the list of all-time great receivers. It’s more than just what people see out here, it's putting in the work when no one is else is,” said Bowman. Shelby completed its third straight 10-0 season. Despite the program’s strong history, it the first time the Whippets posted three consecutive 10-0 regular seasons. Bowman was a starter on all three teams. “It hasn’t set in yet, and I bet a lot of kids would want to have this moment. I'm truly grateful,” said Bowman. Shelby head coach Rob Mahaney knows the significance of tonight’s accolades. “These seniors are going to graduate going 30-0 in the regular season. That’s pretty special. The amount of high school football players that can say that has to be really small,” Mahaney said. Last week, Shelby survived an upset scare at Pleasant. In Week 10, Shelby wasted no time getting to it. Harding was unable to recover an onside kick on the opening play. Then, just two plays later quarterback Michael Shepherd ran in an eight-yard touchdown. The Whippets called Shepherd’s number again on a 1-yard score later in the first quarter as well. Gavin Baker and Luke Blevins each found themselves in the endzone by the end of the night. Shepherd connected with Bowman on a 46-yarder for the final score, which came in the third quarter before Bowman’s night was over. Shepherd threw for 228 yards and ran for 52. The running back duo was tough as usual. Baker ran for 59, and Blevins added 46. Marion Harding’s best possession occurred when Jackson Payne returned a kickoff to Shelby’s 37-yard line. But that drive ended with a Braydon Ream sack on fourth down. Quarterback Dez Feliciano finished the night 15-of-30 passing for 217 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. His favorite target was Jaden Jordan, who finished with 4 receptions for 62 yards. Harding’s lone touchdown came on a 10-yard touchdown reception by Marcus McGary with 6 minutes left in the fourth quarter. The Presidents finish the 2026 season at 5-5. The Shelby defense allowed just 10 total yards rushing. Casyn Koch returned an interception 21 yards with 5:15 to go in the second quarter to make it 28-0 at that point. Shelby has clinched a bye and will most likely be the OHSAA Division IV Region 14 No. 2 seed, according to JoeEitel.com “It’s a full circle moment to me because these are the kids that were the little brothers of the players when I first came here. You hope that they’ve now in

But that drive ended with a Braydon Ream sack on fourth down. Quarterback Dez Feliciano finished the night 15-of-30 passing for 217 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. His favorite target was Jaden Jordan, who finished with 4 receptions for 62 yards. Harding’s lone touchdown came on a 10-yard touchdown reception by Marcus McGary with 6 minutes left in the fourth quarter. The Presidents finish the 2026 season at 5-5. The Shelby defense allowed just 10 total yards rushing. Casyn Koch returned an interception 21 yards with 5:15 to go in the second quarter to make it 28-0 at that point. Shelby has clinched a bye and will most likely be the OHSAA Division IV Region 14 No. 2 seed, according to JoeEitel.com “It’s a full circle moment to me because these are the kids that were the little brothers of the players when I first came here. You hope that they’ve now inspired the next generation. Somebody asked me why Shelby is so special recently, and I think it's the community. It’s pride that the alumni have, the people that live in this town,” Mahaney added. This article originally appeared on Mansfield News Journal: Bowman makes Ohio history as Shelby cruises to third straight 10-0 season

item.title: Atlanta Hawks put NBA on notice with historic 47-point beatdown of Hornets
item.description: Atlanta Hawks put NBA on notice with historic 47-point beatdown of Hornets originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Hawks delivered a statement performance Friday night, dominating the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 at Spectrum Center to improve to 2-0 on the young NBA season. Atlanta's 47-point victory marked the largest winning margin in franchise history, surpassing its previous record of 46 points against Sacramento in 2017. More importantly, the Hawks demonstrated how dangerous they can become when their defense matches their offensive firepower. Jalen Johnson led Atlanta with 19 points, seven rebounds and eight assists, while Aaron Wiggins provided an impressive spark off the bench with 19 points on 7-of-9 shooting. The Hawks established control early behind CJ McCollum, who scored 11 first-quarter points. Atlanta's defensive pressure disrupted Charlotte's offensive rhythm, creating turnovers and transition opportunities. Atlanta carried a commanding 68-43 advantage into halftime, leaving the Hornets searching for answers. Dyson Daniels continued making his presence felt defensively, recording four steals in the third quarter. His relentless pressure helped Atlanta limit Charlotte to just 19 points during the period. The Hawks entered the fourth quarter leading 97-62, allowing their reserves to finish the contest while the starters received valuable rest. Nickeil Alexander-Walker contributed 14 points, while Daniels finished with 11 points and nine rebounds. Charlotte struggled offensively throughout the night, shooting just 34% from the field. Naz Reid led the Hornets with 17 points, while Brandon Miller managed only six points. Atlanta forced 27 turnovers and converted those mistakes into 25 points, highlighting its defensive dominance. The performance represented a significant improvement defensively after Atlanta surrendered 125 points in Wednesday's season-opening victory over Orlando. For the Hawks, the early results suggest this team has the offensive balance, defensive intensity and bench production necessary to compete in the Eastern Conference. Atlanta will look to maintain its undefeated start Saturday night when it hosts the Houston Rockets in its home opener. The challenge now is sustaining that intensity against tougher competition as the season progresses. item.title: Eminem's Mom's Spaghetti heading to Ford Field for Sunday's Lions game
item.description: Eminem's Mom's Spaghetti is making its Ford Field debut. The Detroit rapper's spaghetti spot — named after a line in his iconic, Oscar-winning 2002 single "Lose Yourself" — will be available at Ford Field during the Detroit Lions game on Oct. 25, during which the Lions take on the Green Bay Packers. The announcement was made Oct. 23 via social media. View this post on Instagram "First it was from the D 2 ur kitchen, now it’s 2 the den! 🦁🍝," read the post, which featured a shadowy figure entering Ford Field and lighting up a Mom's Spaghetti neon sign. "Mom’s Spaghetti x Ford Field, 10/25." The dish — "more homespun than chef-driven," according to a 2021 Detroit News review — will be served outside Section 127, which sits at roughly the 50-yard line on the visitor's side of the field, on the building's north side. Mom's Spaghetti opened its permanent location in Sept. 2021 , in the alley between Union Assembly and the Fillmore Detroit. The Rock and Roll Hall of Famer first brought Mom's Spaghetti to life at a pop-up at the Shelter in Detroit in 2017 . During the COVID-19 pandemic, servings of the signature spaghetti were served to frontline workers at several area hospitals . Mom's Spaghetti merchandise in Detroit Lions' colors was introduced in 2024 . It's not the Lions' only taste of Mom's Spaghetti this season. Earlier this week, it was announced the saucy pasta fare would be served from a pop-up food truck during the Lions' Munich Fan Fest Nov. 13-14, which precedes the team's Nov. 15 game in Germany against the New England Patriots. Eminem has an ongoing partnership with the Detroit Lions to produce the team's halftime show at its annual Thanksgiving game. That deal started last year — and saw Eminem performing with Jack White — and runs through 2027 . Halftime plans for the Nov. 26 game have not been announced. Also this week, it was announced that Eminem's influencer daughter, Hailie Jade, is set to host a tailgate party at Union Assembly on Nov. 1, prior to the Lions' matchup with the Minnesota Vikings. Naturally, the party will be serving up helpings of Mom's Spaghetti, it was announced in a release. Kickoff for Sunday's game at Ford Field is 4:25 p.m. agraham@detroitnews.com This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Eminem's Mom's Spaghetti heading to Ford Field for Sunday's Lions game

While Lone’er Kavanagh prefers a measured, technical point-fighting pace, Temirov thrives on turning bouts into chaotic firefights in the pocket. By cutting off the cage aggressively and throwing in heavy three- and four-punch combinations, he can trap the faster mover against the fence. Additionally, Temirov has shown improved patience and three-round conditioning, proven by recent wins over seasoned veterans like Steve Erceg and Charles Johnson. He also holds an undefeated takedown defense rate in the promotion and can mix in timely level changes of his own to disrupt a striker’s rhythm. If Temirov invests early in body shots and forces Kavanagh to trade in close quarters, his durability and heavy hands will take over. He will catch Kavanagh during an exchange, hurt him along the cage, and secure an impactful win. Final Lone’er Kavanagh-Ramazan Temirov Prediction & Pick This flyweight clash is a classic matador-versus-bull matchup between the slick outside movement of Lone’er Kavanagh and the explosive pocket power of Ramazan Temirov. Temirov will immediately march forward looking to trap his taller opponent along the fence and unload his signature hooks. However, Kavanagh already proved against elite opposition that he has the composure and footwork to navigate heavy pressure without panicking. Utilizing athree-inch reach advantage, the Englishman will establish his jab and punish Temirov’s lead leg every time the Uzbek fighter plants his feet to swing. Temirov will have dangerous moments in the opening frame when he closes the gap, forcing Kavanagh to respect his power and stay on his bicycle. As the bout progresses into the second and third rounds, though, Temirov’s wide swings will begin to miss the mark against a constant moving target. Kavanagh will pick his shots cleanly from the outside, counter effectively, and secure a unanimous decision victory. Final Lone’er Kavanagh-Ramazan Temirov Prediction & Pick: Lone’er Kavanagh (-115), OVER 2.5 Rounds (-120) Related: Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev prediction, odds, pick for UFC 333 Related: Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili prediction, odds, pick for UFC 333

item.title: Highlights! Huge underdog Michael Caliendo upsets Jordan Burroughs at RAF 14
item.description: One of the bigger upsets in Real American Freestyle (RAF) history just went down. Massive +550 betting underdog Michael Caliendo stunned American wrestling legend Jordan Burroughs earlier tonight (Fri., Oct. 23, 2026), defeating the Olympic gold medalist 8-5 at RAF 14 inside Fontainebleau Las Vegas in Las Vegas, Nevada. And Caliendo didn’t steal the win with one lucky exchange—he outwrestled Burroughs for most of the match. The four-time NCAA All-American looked approximately three times faster than the 38-year-old legend during the opening two periods, beating Burroughs to positions, escaping danger and frustrating him with constant movement. By the time the final frame began, Caliendo had built a commanding 5-0 advantage and was minutes away from pulling off the unthinkable. Burroughs finally found his vintage explosion in the third period and began mounting what appeared to be another legendary comeback. The six-time World champion increased his pressure, forced Caliendo backward and rapidly erased most of the deficit. But Caliendo refused to collapse. Instead of panicking as Burroughs came storming back, the former Iowa Hawkeye remained composed, defended the American icon’s late attacks and found enough offense of his own to secure the massive 8-5 upset. View this post on Instagram Burroughs closed as an enormous -800 betting favorite, while Caliendo entered at +550. The result is easily the biggest win of Caliendo’s young career. The former Iowa standout finished as the NCAA runner-up at 165 pounds in 2026, completing his collegiate career as a four-time All-American and two-time national finalist. Burroughs, meanwhile, entered RAF 14 with plenty of momentum after dominating UFC Welterweight contender Sean Brady and Magomed Kurbanaliev in his first two appearances with the promotion. The 2012 Olympic champion had also been openly considering another Olympic run in 2028. At 38 years old, Burroughs remains one of the greatest American wrestlers ever—but on Friday night, youth and speed finally caught him. For complete RAF 14 results, coverage, and highlights click HERE .

item.title: Is Mikal Bridges Playing Tonight? Why Knicks’ Star Scored 0 First-Half Points
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 08: Mikal Bridges #25 of the New York Knicks in action against the Washington Wizards at Madison Square Garden on October 08, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty The New York Knicks are playing their second game of the season on Friday night. You might not realize that Mikal Bridges is even out there if you just look at the stat sheet, though. The Knicks lost a tough game in their opener on Tuesday when the Philadelphia 76ers rallied past them to win late. Now, New York is trying to bounce back in another marquee game, playing in Boston against the Celtics. Bridges isn’t helping the cause much at all. Is Mikal Bridges Playing Tonight? Yes, Mikal Bridges is active and healthy and playing tonight for the Knicks. He just was shut out in the first half. He scored zero points before the intermission. The Knicks trailed at the half, 50-49. Karl-Anthony Towns led the way with 12 points. OG Anunoby and Miles McBride each had eight points. Josh Hart and Jalen Brunson each had seven points. Bridges had 0. Why Doesn’t Mikal Bridges Have Any Points? Bridges simply hasn’t had any first half success putting the ball in the basket. He missed all four field goals he attempted in the first half. All four tries were from 3-point range. He wasn’t in attack mode at all, not taking a 2 or getting to the line. Bridges is often a smooth midrange shooter, too, but he didn’t get to any of those spots, either. Bridges had limited contributions elsewhere on the floor. He had two assists, a rebound, a steal and a turnover in the first half. Mikal Bridges Stats This slow start in the first half followed up a terrible opener for Bridges. He played 33 minutes in their opening loss to the 76ers and made just 2-of-8 shots. He was 0-for-2 from 3 and didn’t attempt a free throw. That added up to four points. He also had three rebounds, one assist and one block. Bridges averaged 14.4 points per game last season and has averaged 13 points or more per game in every year dating back to 2020-21. He’s also a great defender and doesn’t have to score to have an impact — but it sure would help the Knicks if Bridges made a shot every once in a while. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Is Mikal Bridges Playing Tonight? Why Knicks’ Star Scored 0 First-Half Points appeared first on HEAVY .

Once back at kicking range, Volkov’s volume and reach advantage will be decisive as he batters Kuniev’s body and head with straight punches. Kuniev is durable enough to survive the barrage, but Volkov’s consistent output at distance will win the rounds. The pick is Volkov by unanimous decision. item.title: Plymouth's 8-man football dream season continues after playoff berth
item.description: PLYMOUTH — Back during the second week of August, it was all a pipe dream. It was when the Plymouth football program was trying to decide what was next. It was battling dangerously low participation numbers and a young roster that wasn’t safe to play a full 11-man football season in the Firelands Conference. HOW'D WE DO? WEEK 10 PICKS All tied up with one week of high school football left Fast forward to Friday, Oct. 23 and the pipe dream became a reality after the Big Red knocked off Kennedy Catholic 34-0 to clinch a 5-5 regular season and snag one of the four 8-man football playoff spots. It will be the first Week 11 game for the Big Red since 2021. “It was a pipe dream all the way up to Week 5 when we lost to McKinley,” Plymouth coach John Gillum said. “It kind of felt like the sky was falling and it was all kind of for nothing. Then, we had a long talk on a Saturday morning and the guys responded. We got healthy and got to play three straight home games and the guys bought into everything we were saying back in August and committed to each other. "Now, we are here.” The Big Red did it with a balanced offensive attack led by sophomore quarterback Weston Kamann who completed 5-of-8 passes for 90 yards and two touchdowns to go with a two-yard TD run. Lincoln Distl had three catches for 56 yards and a score and Isaiah Miller added a two-yard TD catch to go with his 88 rushing yards and two scores on nine carries. Keegan Beverly added a 32-yard catch and 42 yards rushing on offense and picked off three passes on defense. They also did it with a stingy defense that allowed just 201 yards of total offense with much of it coming late in the game with a running-clock differential. It was the first shutout since Week 1 of last season. “It was really all about just seeing the ball and attacking it,” Beverly said. “If I see the ball go up, I am going to go get it. That is just the mindset I have to have for my team.” The Big Red started the 2026 season going from unsure if there would even be football played on Alumni Field to joining the Northern 8 Conference as an 8-man football member to winning their first-ever 8-man football game then losing their next four to go 1-4 at the midway point of the season. "Now, we are here.” The Big Red did it with a balanced offensive attack led by sophomore quarterback Weston Kamann who completed 5-of-8 passes for 90 yards and two touchdowns to go with a two-yard TD run. "It has been awesome to be a part of.” Beverly agrees. “We started off the season slow and it was rough, but the entire team got together and decided to lock in,” Beverly said. “We started our winning streak against Chalker and we just kept building momentum. Now, here we are, getting ready to play in Week 11. “It feels so good. We had only won four games the past three seasons and now, we have surpassed that in one year. That is amazing. We definitely feel a lot of momentum and we hope we can keep it going in all sports this year and in the future. This sophomore class is going to carry on what we started.” Before the season started, Gillum was in a dark place after seeing a program he cares so much about be forced into 8-man football action. But something switched during the weeks of preparation leading up to that first game. “It was all worth it once we found out that it was still going to feel like football and we saw all the seniors and underclassmen were going to make special memories,” Gillum said. “It’s why we want football to exist. That was when I knew it was all worth it.” And it is absolutely worth it after the Big Red clinched a playoff spot. “It did feel impossible,” Gillum said. “I wasn’t really focused on the standings and none of it was even crossing my mind until the Danbury game and when we pulled that one out, we started really believing in Week 11.” And that belief hit an all-time high on Thursday night, the night before the Week 10 win. “It started last night with our end-of-the-year youth flag football night under the lights,” Gillum said. “After all the little kids left, we still had every single varsity player on the field playing catch with each other for another 45 minutes. It’s awesome to be a part of this.” This article originally appeared on Mansfield News Journal: Plymouth's 8-man football dream season continues after playoff berth

item.title: Returning Steffey leads West Lafayette football to sectional win
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE — Kojo Steffey texted coach Shane Fry on Monday that he was heading to the doctor’s office. At 2:30 p.m., he was cleared to play football. Fry had no idea it could even be a possibility. Steffey, who had been out with a leg injury since Sept. 18’s game against Logansport, wasn’t expected to return for West Lafayette this season. But sure enough, Steffey showed up at 4 p.m. for practice that same day and began to ramp up for a return. To help lead the Red Devils to a 49-14 victory over Northwestern in the quarterfinals of Class 3A, Sectional 28 on Friday, Oct. 23, Steffey scored three touchdowns and rushed for 148 yards on 12 carries. It was like he never skipped a beat, despite even surprising himself with his play. “This whole week I’ve been training (and) I’ve been practicing, it felt amazing,” Steffey said. “I didn’t think I was about to come out and do this, but it feels great.” More: Lafayette area IHSAA football sectional quarterfinal scores, updates It wasn’t for certain that Steffey would start until Friday. One of the other two options at running back was sick, and with the senior assuring Fry that he was good to go, it was decided that he would get the nod. It didn’t take long for him to showcase why. Steffey put West Lafayette (3-7) on the board initially at the 8:31 mark of the first quarter. After converting a fourth-and-4 opportunity, he followed it up by bringing in a touchdown from a few yards out. Then at the start of the second, he got the ball to the 1-yard line on a 9-yard rush to set up a touchdown for Chase Ostrom to grab a 14-0 lead. But the defining moment of his comeback was yet to happen. With 8:03 to go in the second quarter, Steffey got loose for an emphatic 65-yard touchdown to go up 21-0. At that moment, it was clear this was West Lafayette’s game to win. Q2, 8:03: West Lafayette 21, Northwestern 0 Steffey breaks through for a 65-yard touchdown…talk about a comeback. Missed the play, but safe to say West Lafayette is feeling good in this one. pic.twitter.com/pKHUL9yyoY — Chase Gemes (@chasegemes) October 23, 2026 “I trust my offensive line 100%,” Steffey said of the play. “Down the gap, I found a hole and took it. Honestly, I thought I was about to get caught, I turned around and I didn’t know he was that far behind. But it felt great.” It was initially Week 1 that Steffey had started to deal with the injury. He toughed it out for a few more weeks, but it eventually forced him to the sideline. But it never kept him out of practice or away from the team; he’s been the first to cheer his team during games and help the running backs around him improve. Much of the season hasn’t gone the way the Red Devils would’ve liked. But that didn’t stop Steffey from wanting to return for a postseason push in his final year. “He could have easily folded up shop and just kind of been done, but he did the opposite,” Fry said. “He’s a captain, and he showed it. So proud of him and I’m so happy that he gets to come out an

Missed the play, but safe to say West Lafayette is feeling good in this one. pic.twitter.com/pKHUL9yyoY — Chase Gemes (@chasegemes) October 23, 2026 “I trust my offensive line 100%,” Steffey said of the play. “Down the gap, I found a hole and took it. Honestly, I thought I was about to get caught, I turned around and I didn’t know he was that far behind. But it felt great.” It was initially Week 1 that Steffey had started to deal with the injury. He toughed it out for a few more weeks, but it eventually forced him to the sideline. But it never kept him out of practice or away from the team; he’s been the first to cheer his team during games and help the running backs around him improve. Much of the season hasn’t gone the way the Red Devils would’ve liked. But that didn’t stop Steffey from wanting to return for a postseason push in his final year. “He could have easily folded up shop and just kind of been done, but he did the opposite,” Fry said. “He’s a captain, and he showed it. So proud of him and I’m so happy that he gets to come out and play at all, let alone have a good game. Even if he had five carries for 10 yards, I would have been thrilled.” Across the board, West Lafayette showed that its team is still bought in despite the rough patches during the year. Quarterback Blake Biddle finished the night completing 20 of 27 passes for 186 passing yards and two touchdowns, finding Braylon Crisp for a 4-yard touchdown and Andrew Pfeiffer down the field for 40 yards. Chase Ostrom, who is the backup signal-caller and a defensive back, connected with Tanner McPherson for a 12-yard touchdown. Ostrom certainly made his presence known on the defensive end. He finished the game with two interceptions, one in the second quarter and one in the third. The Red Devils as a unit snagged four interceptions, including Onyx Shamo adding one in the third. They had even more that were called back due to penalties. More: 'Mature' West Lafayette volleyball team looking to breakthrough regionals More: Faith Christian boys soccer feeling 'less pressure' heading into semi-state Max Smosna tallied a fumble recovery as well, who has been a boost in the secondary splitting time at safety throughout the year. All in all, West Lafayette feels good about how the secondary has progressed. “The defensive backs have had games where they’ve struggled at times,” Fry said. “But they do a great job at, like everybody else, learning from it and coming back and getting better each week.” As much as the ups and downs have been an issue for the Red Devils on the field, the pieces are starting to click at the opportune time in the year. It was the most complete game they’ve played all season, and they’ll need that again next week against Maconaquah (9-0) at home in the semifinals. It’s a rematch from two years ago in the sectional championship, in which West Lafayette fell 17-14 in a heartbreaking loss. It’ll be a considerably tougher out than Northwestern (4-6), but it’s ready for the fight. “We’ve got to keep our head on straight and watch the film,” Fry said. “I think our guys are up to the challenge. We love that it’s going to be a home game. It’ll be fun.” Steffey experienced that loss to Maconaquah. Grouped with that, battling injury and losing more games than winning this year, there’s a lot of motivation for him and the Red Devils to have next week. “We all think we can definitely go to a sectional championship this year,” Steffey said. “We want it so bad after the tough season everyone’s had.” At 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 30, in West Lafayette, they’ll get the chance to exorcise those demons. Chase Gemes covers high school sports and Purdue women's basketball for the Journal & Courier. He can be reached at cgemes@usatodayco.com. This article originally appeared on Lafayette Journal & Courier: Returning Steffey leads West Lafayette football to sectional win

With Keita stepping in on short notice to replace Arnold Allen, the European standout has not had a full training camp tailored specifically for a relentless wrestler of Pico’s caliber. Historically, Aaron Pico’s biggest vulnerability has been his chin and his tendency to get drawn into reckless firefights, with all five of his career defeats coming by way of stoppage. Even when Pico intends to wrestle, he often enters range behind aggressive combinations with his head on the centerline. Keita thrives against aggressive forward pressure, using his two-inch reach advantage and quick footwork to create collision knockouts as opponents step in. Pico will survive the early speed of Keita, ground him consistently across three rounds, and win a unanimous decision. item.title: Rockets Announced Reed Sheppard Injury Designation vs. Spurs
item.description: Houston Rockets guard Reed Sheppard is unlikely to play Friday after picking up a knee injury in Wednesday's win over the Dallas Mavericks, says head coach Ime Udoka. Getty Houston Rockets guard Reed Sheppard was initially listed as questionable for Friday’s game against the San Antonio Spurs. Sheppard picked up a knee injury in Wednesday’s win over the Dallas Mavericks. Heading into Friday’s matchup, Sheppard appears to be leaning toward sitting out of Houston’s game against the Spurs. Rockets head coach Ime Udoka said Reed Sheppard is “unlikely to play tonight after bumping his knee” in the win over Dallas. It will be the first game Sheppard has missed since the 2024-25 season. The 22-year-old appeared in all 82 games for the Rockets last season. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Rockets Announced Reed Sheppard Injury Designation vs. Spurs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Philo tops Maysville, shares MVL title as Lincicome ties record
item.description: NEWTON TOWNSHIP — A strong running game and a stout defense — trademarks of Dirk Lincicome's tenure at Philo. Both elements played vital roles in Friday's 27-13 win over Maysville, as the Electrics' head coach tied the legendary Sam Hatfield with 106 career wins on the Philo sidelines. The Electrics earned a share of the Muskingum Valley League Big School Division title with Sheridan and Tri-Valley, as all three finished 4-1. Lincicome will also have a chance to break the record in Week 11, as playoff pairings are announced on Sunday. "Sam Hatfield is a legend and a man who I respect beyond words," Lincicome said. "This is something I never dreamed of. There's no comparison between me and him, including his years of service where he coached three teams and served as AD (athletic director) at the same time. "I'm just fortunate to be here and lucky enough to have a lot of good players and coaches on my side. I'm just carrying the torch for the next coach." Slade Sprankle had another stellar night, running for 261 yards and four touchdowns on 45 carries, while the Philo defense forced three turnovers and made several key stops. "We told our kids coming in that we still had a lot in front of us. I wanted to see how bad we wanted it and if we could finish strong," Lincicome said. "Maysville has a lot of weapons on offense, and we reminded our kids at halftime that they were going to fight until the end. We got a couple takeaways and some stops inside the 20. We limited their opportunities, and those moments turned the momentum our way."
