item.title: It happened again! Michigan hockey stuns WMU with 0.1 seconds left
item.description: Stop us if you've heard this before. With 0.1 seconds left on the clock — yes, again — Michigan beat Western Michigan, this time in hockey, when Will Horcoff scored with a single tick left in regulation in a battle of top-five teams at Yost Ice Arena on Friday, Oct. 23. Horcoff's goal gave No. 1 Michigan a 3-2 victory over No. 5 Western Michigan. It was the second time in a month-and-a-half that Michigan beat Western Michigan with 0.1 seconds left on the clock, after the football team did it on a Hail Mary touchdown for a 13-12 win at Michigan Stadium on Sept. 5. That was a controversial finish, given clock discrepancies between what was seen on the stadium scoreboard and TV and what replay officials saw in putting that one second on the clock and giving Michigan one more play. There was no controversy with Friday night's hockey finish, but there was just as much drama, as the Wolverines scored three third-period goals to stay undefeated at 7-0 on a night when Michigan paid tribute to the 1996 NCAA championship team before a sellout crowd of 5,800. "Different sport, same ending," Michigan hockey's X account posted Friday night, with a fist-bump emoji. UM beats WMU with 0.1 seconds left on the clock. Seriously. https://t.co/5hwlRgQhz8 — Tony Paul | Detroit News (@TonyPaul1984) October 24, 2026 Western Michigan (4-1) took a 1-0 lead in the second period when senior forward Zaccharya Wisdom scored. Michigan answered back early in the third period, when senior forward Jayden Perron scored his 10th goal of the season. Twenty-two seconds later, junior defenseman Dakoda Rheaume-Mullen (Northville) scored to give the Wolverines a 2-1 lead. Western Michigan senior forward William Whitelaw, who previously played at Michigan, got some revenge against his former mates when he scored the tying goal, a short-handed goal, at 8 minutes, 45 seconds into the third period. It looked like the game was almost certainly heading to overtime — until Horcoff, a junior forward from Birmingham, fired off the improbable winner, beating Western Michigan sophomore goalie Quentin Miller over his right shoulder. That set off a raucous celebration at Yost. Officials reviewed the goal to make sure it did, in fact, beat the clock, and they ruled that it, indeed, was good. This time, the officials' clock ruling was correct, unlike in football, when the Wolverines shouldn't have been allotted that final play, the NCAA later acknowledged. Western Michigan and Michigan meet again in hockey Saturday, Jan. 30, on the football field (how fitting is that). They will play at Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo, in an outdoor hockey showcase. tpaul@detroitnews.com @tonypaul1984 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: It happened again! Horcoff's goal gave No. 1 Michigan a 3-2 victory over No. 5 Western Michigan. It was the second time in a month-and-a-half that Michigan beat Western Michigan with 0.1 seconds left on the clock, after the football team did it on a Hail Mary touchdown for a 13-12 win at Michigan Stadium on Sept. 5. That was a controversial finish, given clock discrepancies between what was seen on the stadium scoreboard and TV and what replay officials saw in putting that one second on the clock and giving Michigan one more play. There was no controversy with Friday night's hockey finish, but there was just as much drama, as the Wolverines scored three third-period goals to stay undefeated at 7-0 on a night when Michigan paid tribute to the 1996 NCAA championship team before a sellout crowd of 5,800. "Different sport, same ending," Michigan hockey's X account posted Friday night, with a fist-bump emoji. UM beats WMU with 0.1 seconds left on the clock. Seriously. https://t.co/5hwlRgQhz8 — Tony Paul | Detroit News (@TonyPaul1984) October 24, 2026 Western Michigan (4-1) took a 1-0 lead in the second period when senior forward Zaccharya Wisdom scored. Michigan answered back early in the third period, when senior forward Jayden Perron scored his 10th goal of the season. Twenty-two seconds later, junior defenseman Dakoda Rheaume-Mullen (Northville) scored to give the Wolverines a 2-1 lead. Western Michigan senior forward William Whitelaw, who previously played at Michigan, got some revenge against his former mates when he scored the tying goal, a short-handed goal, at 8 minutes, 45 seconds into the third period. It looked like the game was almost certainly heading to overtime — until Horcoff, a junior forward from Birmingham, fired off the improbable winner, beating Western Michigan sophomore goalie Quentin Miller over his right shoulder. That set off a raucous celebration at Yost. Officials reviewed the goal to make sure it did, in fact, beat the clock, and they ruled that it, indeed, was good. This time, the officials' clock ruling was correct, unlike in football, when the Wolverines shouldn't have been allotted that final play, the NCAA later acknowledged. Western Michigan and Michigan meet again in hockey Saturday, Jan. 30, on the football field (how fitting is that). They will play at Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo, in an outdoor hockey showcase. tpaul@detroitnews.com @tonypaul1984 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: It happened again! Michigan hockey stuns WMU with 0.1 seconds left

item.title: NFL predictions: Jets, Aaron Glenn face a must win game against winless Dolphins
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 7: Isaiah Williams #18 of the New York Jets runs with the football during the second quarter against the Miami Dolphins at MetLife Stadium on December 7, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey to take on the Miami Dolphins in the Jets’ seventh game of the 2026 season. The Jets will be looking to get back on the winning track after dropping a hard fought game on the road against the New England Patriots last week. These two teams last met in a 34 – 10 Dolphins thrashing of the Jets last December. The Dolphins have won six of the last seven and 16 of the last 20 games between these two teams. The Dolphins lead the overall series 63 – 57 – 1. With the Dolphins clearly tanking this season in hopes of a top draft pick in 2027, they have opened their 2026 campaign with five straight losses. If the Jets can’t beat this team at home, Aaron Glenn’s seat as head coach of the New York Jets will be incendiary. Let’s make a few predictions for the game on Sunday. The Jets hold the Dolphins offense under 150 passing yards and under 250 total yards. The Jets defense forces at least two Dolphins turnovers. No Dolphins receiver has more than 50 receiving yards in the game. At no point in the second half do the Dolphins get closer than a touchdown to the Jets. Geno Smith passes for 250+ yards, 2+ touchdowns and 0 interceptions. The Jets cruise to a 27 – 13 victory. These predictions are just for fun. Betting based on some random dude on the internet having some fun would be very poor judgment and can be hazardous to your financial health. If you choose to bet on the game, make your own calls. item.title: Berlin Brothersvalley holds off North Star in duel of top ICC programs
item.description: BERLIN — Senior Corbin Kordell picked off two Kasey Yoder passes and sealed the victory with a 42-yard reception on a third-down play, helping Berlin Brothersvalley past North Star 17-14, in a showdown of Inter-County Conference South programs, Friday, Oct. 23. "It's great to get the 1-seed (in the District 5-2A playoffs)," said Kordell. "It's been a while since Berlin's had this many wins. It is great to do things the Berlin way and have 41 people around me that believe the same way as me." Week 9 highlights. Pa. high school football, Somerset County Week 9 live score updates Week 9 previews Berlin Brothersvalley, North Star clash with plenty at stake in Week 9 The win puts Berlin Brothersvalley in the driver seat in D5-2A as well as the ICC South. Junior running back Carter Durst tallied 131 rushing yards and two touchdowns for the Mountaineers. Berlin Brothersvalley (8-1) limited Yoder to 143 rushing yards and a touchdown on 23 carries as well as 102 passing yards and a TD. Berlin Brothersvalley won the battle in the trenches against a bigger North Star front. "I think it's one of those games, you look at their line, you look at our size over here," Berlin Brothersvalley coach Dante Paul said. "We're not the biggest guys. We're not the most athletic. Whatever it is, but I'm proud of our guys' fight. I told them all year long, if we can match other teams' effort and physicality, we're going to find ourselves in ball games. "When you prepare and execute, good things end up happening." North Star (7-2) struck first on the opening series of the game. Yoder capped a 6-play, 62-yard drive with a 1-yard touchdown run. Sean Hemminger added the PAT for a 7-0 lead with 8:29 to go in the quarter. Berlin Brothersvalley answered to open the second quarter. The Mountaineers took advantage of a short field and a pass interference call against the Cougars on a fourth-down play to keep the drive alive. Durst rumbled 21 yards out of the wildcat to paydirt. Josh Brinton evened the score with the PAT. The Cougars' defense, which has not allowed more than 17 points in a game this season, came up with a fumble recovery by Brody Shroyer and an interception by Louis Lepley in the second to slow any Mountaineer momentum. North Star took over at the Berlin Brothersvalley 38-yard line with 1:28 to go in the half. The Cougars marched down to the 9-yard line, and a penalty on a field goal attempt set them up fourth-and-goal at the 4. Rather than kick the field goal, first-year coach Shane Smith went for it. Yoder's pass was batted away and the game stayed tied at the break. "Berlin's been playing defense like this for 40 years," Smith said. "I thought Kasey spreading them out was our best opportunity to move the ball. When they moved the ball inside the 5, I thought, we are going to the locker room tied or with some serious momentum with a touchdown. Field goals are never guaranteed. "We missed some opportunities in the first half." Durst broke the tie on the first series

Berlin Brothersvalley had a 16-play drive that carried in the fourth quarter, running off 7:19 of game clock in the final frame. Despite failing to convert a fourth down, the defense responded with Kordell's interception defensively and big catch on offense to seal the deal. Adam Ripple is the Daily American sports editor. item.title: Stephen A. Smith says LeBron James ‘deserves better’ after Trump criticism
item.description: Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images Stephen A. Smith has defended LeBron James after Donald Trump criticised the Philadelphia 76ers star over his behaviour during the US national anthem, arguing that the NBA legend should not be judged by a single moment. The ESPN personality acknowledged that James’ actions may not have been well received but insisted his career and conduct as a role model deserved greater consideration. Trump called James a “total disgrace” after footage showed the forward stretching and appearing to mimic a golf swing while the anthem played before Philadelphia’s game against the New York Knicks. Stephen A. Smith pushes back on Donald Trump’s LeBron James criticism Speaking on his YouTube channel, Smith praised James’ standing in basketball and his reputation throughout his career. He said: “LeBron James as a role model, as a champion, is one of the greatest and belongs on the Mount Rushmore of those categories in American, if not world history. That’s how phenomenal he has been. He does not deserve to be viewed as some unpatriotic individual. Not at all.” Smith acknowledged that James’ behaviour during the anthem was open to criticism but argued it should not overshadow his wider achievements. “I’m not here to tell you that it was a good look what LeBron did,” Smith continued. “I’m here to tell you that his history of professionalism, of decorum, and of handling himself like a role model should take precedence over one moment in which he was listening to the national anthem and feigning a golf swing. He deserves better than that from us.” Smith also suggested that Trump’s criticism could serve a political purpose, claiming the president was trying to galvanise public support ahead of the midterm elections. James himself has now responded to the controversy, dismissing the president’s comments after Philadelphia’s comeback victory over Cleveland. “Yeah, yeah, must be a slow news day at the office,” James told reporters. “A slow news day in the office.” The 76ers star recorded 17 points and 10 rebounds in the 114-106 win, helping his new team recover from a 29-point deficit against his former side. Philadelphia coach Nick Nurse also played down the distraction, insisting his priority was keeping the team focused on preparation and performance. With the 76ers making a strong start to the season, James will now be looking to keep the attention on basketball as the team builds momentum. item.title: Hawks’ Dyson Daniels puts on a steal master class against the Hornets
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Hawks’ Dyson Daniels puts on a steal master class against the Hornets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It’s clear to Atlanta Hawks guard Dyson Daniels that his shooting needs major improvement, which is why he spent much of the offseason trying to fix it. However, his big strength remains his defense, and he put that on full display in the Hawks’ 128-81 demolition of the Charlotte Hornets. “The Great Barrier Thief” absolutely tormented the Hornets as he helped himself to seven steals in the game. NBA on ESPN posted a video montage on X, formerly Twitter, highlighting Daniels’ many takeaways. The Great Barrier Thief had 7 steals 😳 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dyson Daniels setting the tone for the Hawks 😤 pic.twitter.com/3F39SzIat3 — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) October 24, 2026 Daniels picked Hornets rookie Christian Anderson’s pocket in the backcourt and intercepted a number of passes to get his seven steals. But while he had good anticipation and awareness, some of the passes the Hornets threw were not very good. The Hornets, who were now without LaMelo Ball , seemed to be missing a steady ballhandler and playmaker to help set up the offense. Aside from his seven steals, Daniels also added 11 points, nine rebounds, and four assists to help the Hawks improve to 2-0 on the season. The two-time NBA All-Defense Team selection is having a strong start to the season with 12 steals over his first two games. However, he has yet to hit a 3-pointer despite working on his shot for much of the offseason. Jalen Johnson and Aaron Wiggins each had 19 points to lead the way for Atlanta, who dealt the Hornets with their heaviest blowout defeat in franchise history. The Hawks will be hoping to extend their perfect start to 3-0 when they host the Houston Rockets in their home opener on Saturday. Related: NBA stars Paolo Banchero, Jalen Johnson have to be seperated after tense end to Hawks-Magic Related: Hawks enter historic Amazon Prime Video partnership for 2026-27 season

item.title: Evangel’s Aiden Carter is a Swiss Army Knife for the Eagles
item.description: If you were Evangel’s Aiden Carter, you would be a very, very tired young man on Saturday morning. That’s the way it is week after week each fall for the multi-talented junior who rarely leaves the football field while making plays that bring Eagle fans to their feet. Against Byrd on Friday (Oct. 23) night, Carter was the deep man on kickoffs, made several outstanding receptions from freshman quarterback Briggs Berlin and picked off a pass late in the first half to stop a potential Byrd scoring drive. All in a night’s work when you’re playing 5A football with a roster that’s more like 2A in size. “Aiden Carter is the type player every successful program needs,” Evangel coach Denny Duron said. “While he could receive plenty of recognition for what he brings to the game of football, it’s the things he does behind the scenes that truly set him apart.” HUNTINGTON WINS: Huntington scores late to slip past Captain Shreve on senior night PREDICTIONS: Find out which Shreveport-area football teams should win Week 8 games Unfortunately for Carter, his effort was in a losing cause as Byrd (1-7) won its first game of the season 28-24 thanks to two 46-yard fourth quarter TD runs by Byrd record-holder Christian Maxie. According to the ECA coaches, Carter leads by example on a daily basis while holding himself and teammates accountable to the standards established in the program. “Aiden is constantly pushing those around him to be better. His leadership is not about attention or recognition — it is about doing what is right and putting the team first,” Duron said. Carter, the eldest son of Evangel assistant coach Fabian Carter, has been known to stay late to turn off the lights after his teammates have departed. He’ll go out of his way to pick up other football players who need a lift. He’s even picked up trash without being asked to do so. “He is usually one of the first players in every meeting and one of the last people to leave campus,” Duron said. “Those small actions may not always show up on a stat sheet, but they are the foundation of a great team. Aiden’s commitment, character and willingness to serve others make him one of the most valuable members of our program. He represents the culture we strive to build and is a true example of what it means to be a leader.” A three-year starter at safety, the 5-foot-11, 203-pound Carter has been a defensive leader for the Eagles since he arrived on campus. Last season, he recorded 55 tackles, including 26 solo, with an interception. His experience, consistency and understanding of the game make him the go-to person for the defense. “Aiden’s football IQ is exceptional, allowing him to quickly recognize formations, understand offensive tendencies, and put himself and his teammates in the right position to make plays,” Duron said. “His leadership, experience, and knowledge of the game will be a major asset as we continue to build one of the top defensive units throughout 2026.” Jimmy Watson covers Louisiana sports

item.title: Kyrie Irving's unique record has now been broken after fouling out against the Pacers
item.description: Kyrie Irving's unique record has now been broken after fouling out against the Pacers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kyrie Irving has always been one of the steadiest players in the league ever since he got drafted in 2011. He will always be reliable in how he plays on offense, and he has a level head whenever he is on the floor. That is apparent because for the first 781 games in his career, he never fouled out of a game. That changed in his 782nd career appearance, as the Dallas Mavericks guard fouled out in the matchup against Tyrese Haliburton and the Indiana Pacers . Kyrie Irving's unique foul record has ended after Mavs vs Pacers The Mavericks were tremendous all night against the Pacers , as Irving led them in scoring with 24 points in only 25 minutes. It was an impressive performance because he also dealt with foul trouble. He held the longest active streak of games played without fouling out. Now, that streak has finally come to an end; it has been noted that only three players exceeded Irving's record in NBA history. Most games played without fouling out across NBA history Wilt Chamberlain 1205 Steve Kerr 1038 Antonio Daniels 952 Kyrie Irving 781 MORE: Kyrie Irving reveals a retirement timeline from basketball It just goes to show that basketball IQ does go a long way. A lot of people don't see it on defense, but Irving still uses his basketball IQ to the highest level on both ends of the floor. That was also the same for both Steve Kerr and Antonio Daniels, who were also cerebral players back in their day. At the end of the day, it does not matter because the Mavericks won their first game of the season. In fact, Irving was in the locker room celebrating new head coach Dusty May's first NBA win . May had some fun with this tidbit because he made a joke about the foul record after the game. "He let the staff know he had never fouled out in a game. Proud to be part of his first," May said after Irving's impressive performance that ended with him fouling for the first time . item.title: Is Desmond Bane Playing Tonight? Why Magic Star Scored 0 First-Half Points
item.description: ORLANDO, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 28: Desmond Bane #3 of the Orlando Magic poses during the 2026 Orlando Magic Media Day at AdventHealth Training Center on September 28, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) Getty The Orlando Magic have an impressive starting lineup. It’s led by their big three of Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane. On Friday night, though, Bane was off the pace. His impact was non-existent in the first half of the Magic’s home matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves. Banchero had 12 points at the break. Wagner and Jalen Suggs each had nine. Bane seemed like he wasn’t even playing. Is Desmond Bane Playing Tonight? Yes, Desmond Bane is active and healthy and playing on Friday night for the Magic against the Timberwolves. He just scored 0 points in the first half. It was a brutal showing for Bane, who spent a lot of time on the court but didn’t find the basket in the first half. Why Didn’t Desmond Bane Score in the First Half? Desmond Bane didn’t score in the first half because he couldn’t make a single shot. He was 0-for-5 from the field, including 0-for-4 from 3-point range. He wasn’t in attack mode. Bane only attempted one 2-pointer, and he didn’t get to the foul line. Bane didn’t even make many other contributions. He had two rebounds and one turnover. It was tough, because Bane played 17 minutes. Some would say he was just out there getting his cardio work in. Desmond Bane Stats Bane got his season off to an OK start in the season opener on Wednesday, although the Magic lost that game 132-125. He had 18 points that night, but he was just at 33% from the floor, including 3-for-10 from 3-point range. Bane added five rebounds, three steals and two assists in the first game of the season. Desmond Bane Trade The reason this matters even more is because the Magic gave up a ton to get Bane in a trade before last season. They sent four unprotected first-round picks, as well as a 2029 first-round pick swap, to the Grizzlies with Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Cole Anthony to acquire Bane. Bane is under contract through the 2028-29 season. The Magic are hoping that he can turn around this cold shooting start to put Orlando in position to contend in the Eastern Conference this season. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Is Desmond Bane Playing Tonight? Why Magic Star Scored 0 First-Half Points appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: RAF 14 results: Mikey Caliendo pulls off massive upset beating Olympic champ Jordan Burroughs
item.description: Mikey Caliendo defied the odds on Friday and scored an impressive win over Olympic champion Jordan Burroughs at RAF 14. While Caliendo has his own credentials, Burroughs is widely considered one of the greatest wrestlers of all-ime and through two matches in RAF he hadn’t allowed a point scored against him. That all changed early in the match when Caliendo attacked right away and snatched a takedown to open the match. Caliendo then began mirroring Burroughs’ movements and at one point even stuffed a blast double leg to maintain his position. By the third period, Caliendo was up 5-0 but Burroughs nearly mounted a comeback when he went on the offensive and starting adding up some points of his own. Caliendo finally counered with another two-point move as Burroughs tried desperately to mount a comeback but time ran out on him. When the match was over the final score read 7-5 with Caliendo getting the victory and handing Burroughs his first loss in RAF. Afterwards, Caliendo celebrated by calling for a title shot. “I don’t care who it is but I want the belt,” Caliendo shouted. It’s a huge win for Caliendo and a surprising setback for Burroughs, who at 38 had still looked as dominant as ever prior to this loss.

item.title: Watch: Brewers’ Jackson Chourio Delivers In 7th Inning Of The World Series (Video)
item.description: Jackson Chourio picked the perfect time to time to come through with a big hit. The Milwaukee Brewers outfielder delivered an RBI single in Game 1 of the World Series on Friday night, giving Milwaukee a 3-1 lead over the Tampa Bay Rays and sending the home crowd into another celebration at American Family Field. For a Brewers team that has waited decades to get back to the Fall Classic, every run feels important. Chourio’s hit gave Milwaukee a little breathing room and put the pressure back on Tampa Bay. The 22-year-old has become one of the most important players on the Brewers ‘ roster, and moments like this are a big reason why. Chourio has the ability to change a game with one swing, and Milwaukee needed that kind of contribution as it looks to get off to a strong start in the World Series. Below is the video. Also Read: Watch: Brewers Pull Off Incredible Strike-‘Em-Out, Throw-‘Em-Out Double Play in World Series Oct 23, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio (11) celebrates after hitting an RBI single against the Tampa Bay Rays during the seventh inning in game one of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Brewers Get a Big Hit From Jackson Chourio Late In Game 1 Of the World Series Chourio’s single was exactly the kind of hit Milwaukee needed. In a World Series game, there is a big difference between holding a narrow lead and giving your pitchers another run to work with. Here is the video: OCTOBER CHOURIO https://t.co/XFmZPF9r0j — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 24, 2026 The Brewers are trying to finish off a remarkable season by winning the first World Series championship in franchise history. They have already taken care of business against the San Diego Padres and Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League playoffs. Now, they are trying to carry that momentum into the biggest series of them all. Tampa Bay is not going to go away quietly, but Chourio’s hit gave Milwaukee an important boost in Game 1. The Brewers still have plenty of baseball left to play, but their young star has already given the home crowd something to celebrate. If Milwaukee is going to bring a championship back to Wisconsin, it will need contributions like this from Chourio and the rest of its lineup. item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.description: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026 Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced. The preparation money for the 32 teams has been more than doubled to $2.5m (£1.86m) each. In 2023, the total preparation money for the tournament was $31m; it will now be $80m. Continue reading...

There has surely never been a greater anti-leadership act in United’s history than Fernandes questioning the man who trusts him to unify the dressing room and execute his on-field plan. item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’

Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
